title: Patologi Anatomi Neurologi

sections.title: Kelainan Kongenital

content.text: CHORISTOMA: Normal tissue growing in an abnormal location. Can be found throughout the body. Example: Leptomeningeal rhabdomyomatosis - striated muscle elements in the cerebellopontine angle region. CYST: Lesion formed as a sac from membranous tissue containing fluid, air, semisolid material, or other substances. CNS cysts include: Colloid cyst (contains colloid fluid), Epidermoid cyst (lined by flattened squamous cells, may contain keratin mass), Arachnoid cyst (contains CSF accumulation).
Choristoma: jaringan normal di lokasi abnormal
Kista Koloid: berisi cairan koloid
Kista Epidermoid: dilapisi sel gepeng, berisi masa keratin
Kista Araknoid: berisi akumulasi cairan CSF

sections.title: Penyakit Serebrovaskular

content.text: INFARK SEREBRI: Brain tissue death caused by disrupted blood flow. Lesions are irreversible; brain cells undergo necrosis. ANEURYSMA INTRAKRANIAL: Dilation or protrusion of cerebral blood vessels due to weakened vessel wall, also called saccular or berry aneurysm. Predominantly located at the Circle of Willis. MALFORMASI VASKULAR: Abnormal vascular connections. EPIDURAL HEMATOMA: Blood collection between skull and dura. SUBDURAL HEMATOMA: Blood collection between dura and arachnoid.
Infark serebri: kematian jaringan otak akibat gangguan aliran darah, irreversible
Aneurysma intracranial: pelebaran pembuluh darah otak, predominant di Circle of Willis
Epidural hematoma: di antara tulang dan duramater
Subdural hematoma: di antara duramater dan arakhnoid

sections.title: Penyakit Infeksi

content.text: DEMYELINATING DISEASE: Loss of myelin sheath causing nerve signal disruption; can form demyelinating pseudotumor lesions. BACTERIAL INFECTION: Brain abscess - microscopically shows purulent necrotic mass bordered by brain parenchyma; etiology includes Streptococcus, Staphylococcus, Clostridium, Mycobacterium tuberculosis. FUNGAL INFECTION (Mycoses): Cryptococcoma; etiology includes Aspergillus, Candida, Histoplasma. PARASITIC INFECTION: Neurocysticercosis (Taenia solium larva in pork); Toxoplasmosis (Toxoplasma gondii from cat feces) - microscopically shows minute basophilic structures containing parasites with surrounding lymphocytes, plasma cells, and macrophages. VIRAL INFECTION: Herpes Simplex encephalitis, Varicella-zoster virus, HIV.
Abses otak: Streptococcus, Staphylococcus, Clostridium, Mycobacterium tuberculosis
Neurosistiserkosis: Taenia solium, larva pada daging babi
Toksoplasmosis: Toxoplasma gondii, ditemukan pada tinja kucing

sections.title: Tumor - Astrositoma

content.text: Astrocytoma is a brain tumor arising from astrocytes. Highly variable depending on location in the CNS, potentially invasive and progressive. Most cases are intracranial; only ~3% are intraspinal. Can occur at all ages, average 35-40 years. Well-differentiated astrocytomas tend to occur in younger patients; anaplastic types more common in middle age. In adults, slightly more common in males. Cerebral hemisphere predilection; in children more commonly in cerebellum. Clinical features depend on location and growth rate. Combination of increased intracranial pressure, progressive neurological deficits, seizures, and cognitive decline is commonly seen. WHO CLASSIFICATION: Grade I (pilocytic astrocytoma, subependymal giant cell astrocytoma); Grade II (diffuse astrocytoma, pleomorphic xanthoastrocytoma, pilomyxoid astrocytoma); Grade III (anaplastic astrocytoma); Grade IV (glioblastoma multiforme). Grade is still best determined by mitotic count.
WHO Grade I: Pilocytic astrocytoma, subependymal giant cell astrocytoma
WHO Grade II: Diffuse astrocytoma, pleomorphic xanthoastrocytoma, pilomyxoid astrocytoma
WHO Grade III: Anaplastic astrocytoma
WHO Grade IV: Glioblastoma multiforme
Grade terbaik tetap berdasarkan jumlah mitosis
Glioblastoma multiforme = WHO Grade IV, most malignant astrocytic tumor

sections.title: Oligodendroglioma dan Meningioma

content.text: OLIGODENDROGLIOMA: Arises from oligodendrocytes. Can be low-grade (WHO Grade II) or high-grade (WHO Grade III/anaplastic). Commonly found in frontal and temporal lobes. Grossly soft, grayish-pink. Contains mineral deposits (calcifications), hemorrhage, and/or cysts. Histology: small round monotonous nuclei, perinuclear halos ('fried egg' appearance), branching thin-walled vessels ('chicken-wire' vessels), microcalcifications (calcospherites). Typically slow-growing, present for years before diagnosis.

MENINGIOMA: Arises from meningothelial cells of the protective meninges. Most common benign brain tumor, slow-growing, usually intracranial but can occur in spinal cord. More common in females, especially adults. Hormonal influence: progesterone receptor expression; tumor size changes during luteal phase and pregnancy. 40-80% have abnormal chromosome 22 at NF2 locus. NF2 is a tumor suppressor gene at 22q12. WHO 2016 classification: Grade I (benign), Grade II (atypical), Grade III (anaplastic). Key histological types: meningepithelial (syncytial), fibroblastic, transitional, psammomatous.
Oligodendroglioma: fried egg appearance, chicken-wire vessels, calcospherites
Meningioma: WHO Grade I (benign), II (atypical), III (anaplastic)
Meningioma: female predominance, progesterone receptor, NF2 association
Oligodendroglioma classic triad: fried egg cells + chicken-wire vessels + calcifications

differential_notes.how_to_separate: Astrocytoma: fibrillary background, no calcifications; Oligodendroglioma: fried egg cells, chicken-wire vessels, calcifications
Meningioma: whorls, psammoma bodies, EMA+; Schwannoma: Antoni A/B areas, Verocay bodies, S100+

red_flags: Rapidly progressive neurological deficits suggesting high-grade tumor
New-onset seizures in adults suggesting neoplasm
Signs of increased intracranial pressure with papilledema
